numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In the univariate smoother path, the smoothed measurement disturbance is returned in the wrong basis: it corresponds to C_t^{-1} eps_t rather than eps_t (can be “off by up to 124”). It also affected FILTER_CONVENTIONAL when the multivariate filter falls back to the univariate approach on singular forecast error covariance F_t. In tests, simulation smoother comparisons were degenerate due to incorrect wiring (variates passed to simulation_smoother() instead of to its simulate() method), leading to comparisons against arrays of zeros.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The smoothed measurement disturbance should be for eps_t. Because transform_diagonalize replaces non-diagonal H_t with diagonal D_t using H_t = C_t D_t C_t', the univariate recursion runs on C_t^{-1} y_t, so the output must be premultiplied by C_t ("Undo the diagonalization: \hat ε_t = C_t \hat ε_t^*"). When the covariance back-transformation cannot be done fully (only the diagonal of Var(C_t^{-1} eps_t) is available while undoing C_t needs off-diagonal elements), the code should warn and document that case instead of silently returning a wrong-basis result.
trigger_conditions: Univariate filtering/smoothing approach is used after diagonalizing a non-diagonal observation covariance H_t via transform_diagonalize (H_t = C_t D_t C_t').
After diagonalization, the univariate recursion output corresponds to C_t^{-1} eps_t; without undoing the diagonalization, the code returns that wrong basis for the smoothed measurement disturbance.
This discrepancy also affects FILTER_CONVENTIONAL because the multivariate filter falls back to the univariate approach on singular forecast error covariance F_t.

Covariance back-transformation cannot be performed the same way when only the diagonal of Var(C_t^{-1} eps_t) is produced; in that case it should warn/document rather than silently return an incorrect-basis covariance.

The test/validation discrepancy could appear when simulation smoother comparisons pass variates to simulation_smoother() instead of to its simulate() method, causing comparisons against arrays of zeros; the fix uses fixed variates. (Execution condition relevant to observing/validating the numerical discrepancy.)

oracle_clues: PR#9979 states transform_diagonalize replaces non-diagonal H_t with diagonal D_t where H_t = C_t D_t C_t' and univariate recursions run on C_t^{-1} y_t; therefore smoothed measurement disturbance must be premultiplied by C_t to recover eps_t.
PR#9979 cites the fix as explicitly undoing the diagonalization using BLAS trmv: \hat ε_t = C_t \hat ε_t^*.

PR#9979 explains that covariance back-transformation cannot be done fully by the same method because univariate recursions only produce the diagonal of Var(C_t^{-1} eps_t); undoing C_t requires off-diagonal elements, so it should warn/document.
PR#9979 provides quantitative oracle evidence for one model: "off by up to 124" before the fix and "1.2e-09 after the fix".
PR#9979 adds a numerical check: y_t = Z_t alpha-hat_t + eps-hat_t holds, which pins the output down without a reference implementation and covers the diffuse path.

category_specific_evidence: The simulation smoother comparisons were incorrectly passing the variates to `simulation_smoother()` rather than to its `simulate()` method, so they were comparing arrays of zeros; with real variates they need the same 1e-7 absolute tolerance as their neighbours.
A numerical property/formula check was added: `y_t = Z_t alpha-hat_t + eps-hat_t` holds, pinning the output down without a reference implementation and covering the diffuse path.

The fix also changes the simulation smoother to be driven by fixed variates and shared across methods, and the univariate test now uses a helper that sets `initial_state_variates=np.zeros(model.k_states)` and generates variates via `rs.normal` for `measurement_disturbance_variates` and `state_disturbance_variates`.
reproduction_risks: If variates are passed to `simulation_smoother()` instead of `simulate()`, the comparison can degenerate to arrays of zeros (invalidates the numerical violation evidence).
Use the same absolute tolerance (1e-7) as the neighbouring comparisons when asserting closeness.
To observe the diffuse-path numerical property violation/coverage, ensure the reproduction includes the diffuse path covered by the `y_t = Z_t alpha-hat_t + eps-hat_t` check.
